hints: Focus on how the polar $\text{H-Br}$ bond and the electron-rich $\text{C=C}$ bond interact at the start of electrophilic addition.
Remember bromine is more electronegative than hydrogen, so identify which end is $\delta^+$ and gets attacked by the pi electrons to form the carbocation and $\text{Br}^-$.
Check the direction of the curly arrows in the second step, the lone pair on the nucleophile must attack the positively charged carbon.
walkthrough:
**Recall the type of mechanism**

Electrophilic addition to an alkene starts with the $\text{C=C}$ pi electrons acting as a nucleophile. They attack the electrophilic ($\delta^+$) end of the polar molecule.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 + \text{H-Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^+ + \text{Br}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$$

**Get the polarity of H-Br right**

Bromine is more electronegative than hydrogen, so the bond is $\text{H}^{\delta+} - \text{Br}^{\delta-}$. The pi bond must attack $\text{H}^{\delta+}$, not $\text{Br}^{\delta+}$.

This gives $\text{H-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2^+$ type intermediate, shown as $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_2^+$ plus $\text{Br}^-$ left behind.

**Check step 1 curly arrows**

The correct arrows are: pi electrons to $\text{H}^{\delta+}$, and $\text{H-Br}$ bond electrons onto $\text{Br}^{\delta-}$ to make $\text{Br}^-$. This rules out any scheme with $\text{Br}^{\delta+}$ and $\text{H}^{\delta-}$.

**Check step 2 curly arrow**

The carbocation is electron deficient and $\text{Br}^-$ is the nucleophile. The arrow must start from the lone pair on $:\text{Br}^-$ and point to the $\text{C}^+$.

An arrow starting from $\text{C}^+$ and pointing to $\text{Br}^-$ is backwards and incorrect. Only one scheme gets both the polarity and both arrows correct.

options.A: Incorrect because the polarity of HBr is reversed as $\text{Br}^{\delta+}-\text{H}^{\delta-}$. The alkene is shown attacking Br, and the second step shows hydride $\text{H}^-$ attacking a bromo-carbocation, which does not happen in HBr addition.
options.B: Correct. Step 1 shows $\text{H}^{\delta+}-\text{Br}^{\delta-}$ with pi electrons attacking $\text{H}^{\delta+}$ to form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^+$ and $\text{Br}^-$. Step 2 shows the lone pair on $:\text{Br}^-$ attacking $\text{C}^+$ to form bromoethane. Both polarities and curly arrows are correct.
options.C: Incorrect because it also reverses the polarity to $\text{Br}^{\delta+}-\text{H}^{\delta-}$. This would imply Br adds first and hydride $\text{H}^-$ adds second, which is chemically wrong for electrophilic addition of HBr.
options.D: Tricky trap. Step 1 has the correct $\text{H}^{\delta+}-\text{Br}^{\delta-}$ polarity and intermediate, but step 2 has the curly arrow backwards, starting from the $\text{C}^+$ instead of from the $:\text{Br}^-$ lone pair. Curly arrows must start from the electron donor.
